gallery.description:
Tombstones in Historic Pioneer Military and Memorial Park in Phoenix, Arizona.
The Cemetery dates back to the 1850s and is located in the area of 15th Ave. and Jefferson St., Phoenix, Arizona.
The main tombstone pictured is that of Florence Esther (August 12, 1878 - June 13, 1909), wife of J. Ernest Walker.
On the National Register of Historic Places in Phoenix, Arizona.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850- William Augustus Hancock.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850- William Augustus Hancock.JPG
gallery.artist: Tony the Marine (talk) / Marine 69-71 at en.wikipedia
gallery.credit: Own work (Original text: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.)
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850- William Augustus Hancock
gallery.description: William Augustus Hancock laid out the first town site of Phoenix in 1870. Known as the "Father of Phoenix", he was appointed District Attorney in 1871, probate judge in 1875 and was the first sheriff in Maricopa County. Hancock died on March 24, 1902. The grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "Knights of Pythias Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-The Rossen Children.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-The Rossen Children.JPG
gallery.artist: Tony the Marine (talk) / Marine 69-71 at en.wikipedia
gallery.credit: Own work (Original text: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.)
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-The Rossen Children
gallery.description: The Rossen Children were the children of Dr. Roland Rosson, owner of the historic Rosson House in Phoenix. Roland Lloyd Rosson died on February 25, 1883 and an "Infant Daughter" on January 7, 1896. The grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "Knights of Pythias Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Millard Raymond
gallery.description: Millard Lee Raymond served as a Rough Rider of Troop F in the Spanish-American War. The grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "Porter Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Robert Plumridge.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Robert Plumridge.JPG
gallery.artist: Tony the Marine (talk) / Marine 69-71 at en.wikipedia
gallery.credit: Own work (Original text: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.)
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Robert Plumridge
gallery.description: Robert Plumridge served in the California Column and fought against the Confederate Forces in the Battle of Picacho Pass during the American Civil War. The grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "Rosedale Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-King S. Woolsey.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-King S. Woolsey.JPG
gallery.artist: Tony the Marine (talk) / Marine 69-71 at en.wikipedia
gallery.credit: Own work (Original text: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.)
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-King S. Woolsey
gallery.description: King S. Woolsey founded one of the first flour mills in the Salt River Valley. He served in various positions in the territorial legislature and opened the first ice skating rink in Phoenix. Woolsey died on June 30, 1879. The grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "City/Loosley Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-John T. Alsap.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-John T. Alsap.JPG
gallery.artist: Tony the Marine (talk) / Marine 69-71 at en.wikipedia
gallery.credit: Own work (Original text: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.)
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-John T. Alsap
gallery.description: John T. Alsap was the first Treasurer of Arizona Territory. He also served as both Speaker of the House and President of the Council in the Arizona Territorial legislature. In 1818, he became the first Mayor of Phoenix. Alsap died September 10, 1886. The grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "Masons Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Jacob the “Dutchman” Waltz.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Jacob the “Dutchman” Waltz.JPG
gallery.credit: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Jacob the “Dutchman” Waltz
gallery.description: Grave site of Jacob "Dutchman" Waltz, a German immigrant who it in the 19th century discovered a gold mine in Arizona and kept its location a secret, hence the "Lost Ducthman's Mine". The grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "Masonic Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The  Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.source: Phoenix-Smurthwaite House-1897-Living room
gallery.description: The living room of the Smurthwaite House which was built in 1897. The house is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street and currently serves as the office of the historic "Pioneer and Military Cemetery" The house was listed in the National Register of Historic Places on May 17, 2001, reference #01000479 (NRHP).

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Czar J. Dyer.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Czar J. Dyer.JPG
gallery.credit: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Czar J. Dyer
gallery.description: Grave site of Czar J. Dyer. Dyer served as Councilman and acting Mayor of Phoenix. Dyer drew the "Bird's Eye view of Phoenix" map which is located in the Smurthwaite House. His grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "Rosedale Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Phillip Darrell Duppa.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Phillip Darrell Duppa.JPG
gallery.credit: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Phillip Darrell Duppa
gallery.description: Grave site of Phillip "Lord" Darrell Duppa, an Englishman who is credited with naming "Phoenix" and "Tempe" and the founding of the town of New River. The grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "Masonic Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Frederick E. Tovrea.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Frederick E. Tovrea.JPG
gallery.credit: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Frederick E. Tovrea
gallery.description: Grave site of Frederick E. Tovrea. Tovrea was the 10 year old son of E. A. Tovrea owner of the "Tovrea Castle" in Phoenix. The child died on July 17, 1898, of a appendicitis.     His grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "A.O.U.W. & K of P  Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Noah M. Broadway.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Noah M. Broadway.JPG
gallery.credit: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Noah M. Broadway
gallery.description: Grave site of Noah M. Broadway who died November 3, 1905. Broadway was one of the original settlers of Phoenix. He was an American Civil War veteran, farmer, and sheriff of Maricopa County. His farm was located between 7th and 23rd Avenues on the south side of what is now "Broadway Road". His grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "Rosedale Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Clarence Proctor.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Clarence Proctor.JPG
gallery.credit: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Clarence Proctor
gallery.description: Grave site of Clarence Proctor, a Buffalo Soldier who was a Sergeant in Troop L of the 10th U.S. Cavalry during the Spanish–American War. On 27 March 1900, Proctor committed suicide at his home in Phoenix. His grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "Porter Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Benjamin Joseph Franklin.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Benjamin Joseph Franklin.JPG
gallery.credit: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-Benjamin Joseph Franklin
gallery.description: Grave site of Benjamin Joseph Franklin. Franklin was a Missouri U.S. Congressman and U.S. Consul to China who in 1896 moved to Arizona. President Grover Cleveland appointed Franklin Arizona's 12th Territorial Governor. Franklin died May 18, 1898. His grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "Rosedale Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.filename: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-John Preston Osborn.JPG
gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-John Preston Osborn.JPG
gallery.credit: I (Tony the Marine (talk)) created this work entirely by myself.
gallery.source: Phoenix-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1850-John Preston Osborn
gallery.description: Grave site of John Preston Osborn. Osborn arrived in Prescott, Arizona in 1854. While he lived there, he built that town's first hotel. Eventually he moved to the Salt River Valley and assisted in the establishment of Phoenix. Osborn died on January 19 1900. Osborn Road in Phoenix is named after him. His grave is located at 1317 W. Jefferson Street in the "A.O.U.W. & K of P  Cemetery" section of Phoenix's historic Pioneer & Military Memorial Park. The Pioneer & Military Memorial Park is listed in the National Register of Historic Places, reference #06001317.

gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Cemetery-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1884-Frank B. Moss.jpg
gallery.credit: Own work
gallery.source: Phoenix-Cemetery-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1884-Frank B. Moss
gallery.description: Grave Frank B. Moss. He was the Mayor, Fire Chief and Wagon Maker of Phoenix. He served two terms in office, the first in 1896 and the second 1905-1906. He died at the age of 53 from a heart attack while serving as mayor, as he ascended the City Hall stairs. He is buried in the I.O.O.F. Cemetery which is located in the Pioneer and Military Memorial Park of Phoenix.

gallery.title: File:Phoenix-Cemetery-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1884-Tom Graham.jpg
gallery.credit: Own work
gallery.source: Phoenix-Cemetery-Pioneer Military and Memorial Park-1884-Tom Graham
gallery.description: Grave of Tom Graham. He was the last man killed in the Pleasant Valley War. Ed Tewsbury ambushed Graham near the Buttes when he was traveling to Tempe with a load of grain. Graham is buried in the A.O.U.W. & K of P Cemeteries which are located in the Pioneer and Military Memorial Park of Phoenix.
